subjectQuote: Clear Creek County Ballot Issue 1 A

whatItDoes:
SHALL CLEAR CREEK COUNTY LODGING TAXES BE INCREASED BY
$800,000.00 ANNUALLY COMMENCING ON JANUARY 1, 2027, AND BY
WHATEVER AMOUNTS ARE RAISED ANNUALLY THEREAFTER, BY
INCREASING THE LODGING TAX RATE FROM TWO PERCENT (2%) TO SIX
PERCENT (6%) ON THE RENTAL FEE, PRICE, OR OTHER CONSIDERATION
PAID OR CHARGED FOR THE LEASING, RENTAL, SALE OR FURNISHING OF
A ROOM OR ACCOMMODATION FOR A SHORT-TERM PERIOD OF LESS
THAN THIRTY (30) CONSECUTIVE DAYS IN CLEAR CREEK COUNTY,
EXCLUDING THE MUNICIPALITY OF THE TOWN OF GEORGETOWN THAT
CURRENTLY HAS ITS OWN ADOPTED LODGING TAX, AND SHALL THE
ALLOCATION OF COUNTY LODGING TAX REVENUE BE MODIFIED SO
THAT THE REVENUE COLLECTED FROM THE SIX PERCENT (6%) COUNTY
LODGING TAX SHALL BE USED AS FOLLOWS:
• UP TO 60% OF THE REVENUE FOR PUBLIC INFRASTRUCTURE
MAINTENANCE OR IMPROVEMENTS; AND ENHANCING PUBLIC
SAFETY MEASURES;
• AT LEAST TWENTY PERCENT (20%) OF THE REVENUE TO PROVIDE
CHILDCARE FOR THE TOURISM-RELATED WORKFORCE,
INCLUDING SEASONAL WORKERS, AND FOR OTHER WORKERS IN
THE COMMUNITY;
• AT LEAST TEN PERCENT (10%) OF THE REVENUE TO PROVIDE
HOUSING FOR THE TOURISM-RELATED WORKFORCE, INCLUDING
SEASONAL WORKERS, AND FOR OTHER WORKERS IN THE
COMMUNITY;
• AT LEAST TEN PERCENT (10%) OF THE REVENUE FOR
ADVERTISING AND MARKETING OF LOCAL TOURISM, AS
REQUIRED BY STATE LAW; AND
WITH ALL SUCH EXPENDITURES SUBJECT TO AN ANNUAL INDEPENDENT
AUDIT AND SPENT IN COMPLIANCE WITH LOCAL GOVERNMENT BUDGET
LAWS, AND SHALL THE FIRST-YEAR REVENUE, AND WHATEVER
ADDITIONAL AMOUNTS ARE RAISED ANNUALLY THEREAFTER, BE
COLLECTED AND SPENT AS A VOTER APPROVED REVENUE CHANGE
NOTWITHSTANDING ANY LIMITATION OR CONDITION UNDER ARTICLE
X, SECTION 20 OF THE COLORADO CONSTITUTION OR ANY OTHER
PROVISION OF LAW?

reviewNotes: The final Resolution R-26-55 expressly states ADOPTED September1,2026, unconditionally certifies this complete question forNovember3,2026, and names Georgetown as excluded from the electorate. It is titled Final in the official meeting attachment list.
The earlier August25survey used$650,000 and other proposal wording. The final operative question authorizes$800,000 and an annual independent audit; the survey text is not used.
Allocations apply to all6%lodging-tax receipts, not only the four-point increase. Infrastructure and safety share a combined maximum60%; other allocations are minimums.

subjectQuote: BALLOT TITLE AND TEXT — BALLOT ISSUE NO. 1B:

whatItDoes:
SHALL MONTEZUMA COUNTY LODGING TAXES BE INCREASED BY
$404,598 IN TAX COLLECTION YEAR 2027 AND BY WHATEVER AMOUNTS
ARE GENERATED ANNUALLY THEREAFTER BY INCREASING THE
COUNTY LODGING TAX FROM 2% TO 5% EFFECTIVE JANUARY 1, 2027,
EXCLUDING THE MUNICIPALITY OF CORTEZ WHICH HAS ITS OWN
LODGING TAX, AND SHALL THE LODGING TAX REVENUES RECEIVED
BY THE COUNTY BE USED FOR THE FOLLOWING PURPOSES:
• TOURISM PROMOTION AND MARKETING;
• RECREATION, OUTDOOR RECREATION, AND VISITOR-RELATED
INFRASTRUCTURE IMPROVEMENTS;
• DESTINATION DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS AND VISITOR EXPERIENCE
ENHANCEMENTS;
• TOURISM RESILIENCY, EMERGENCY RESPONSE, AND RECOVERY
EFFORTS RELATED TO EVENTS AFFECTING VISITATION;
• ADMINISTRATION, OVERSIGHT, AND IMPLEMENTATION OF
AUTHORIZED LODGING TAX PROGRAMS;
AND SHALL THE COUNTY BE AUTHORIZED TO COLLECT, RETAIN, AND
SPEND ALL REVENUES GENERATED BY SUCH TAX AS A VOTER-
APPROVED REVENUE CHANGE UNDER ARTICLE X, SECTION 20 OF THE
COLORADO CONSTITUTION, OR ANY OTHER LAW?

reviewNotes: The prior source-ready pending record is reused with the same stable contestId and neutral prose. Exact county-minus-Cortez geography resolves its attachment; no duplicate question is created.

Current official Cortez sample has county1A and city2A but no lodging1B; all other current county styles contain1B. C.R.S.§30-11-107.5(3)(a),(b)(I) expressly excludes a municipality with its own lodging tax from the county lodging-tax election proposal.
